Front: Relationship between period, frequency, and Hz?
Back: Frequency = 1/period; Hz = cycles per second. A cycle of 0.02 s -> 1/0.02 = 50 Hz. Period and frequency are reciprocals.

Front: What is spectral decomposition, and what are the DFT and the spectrum?
Back: Any signal can be expressed as a sum of sinusoids at different frequencies. The spectrum is that set (which frequencies, at what amplitude/phase). The DFT takes the signal from the time domain to its spectrum in the frequency domain; the FFT is the fast algorithm for the DFT.

Front: Fundamental vs dominant frequency; what are harmonics?
Back: Fundamental = the lowest-frequency component. Dominant = the component with the largest amplitude (can differ from the fundamental). Harmonics = integer multiples of the FUNDAMENTAL (200 -> 400, 600, 800). An octave = a doubling (the 2nd harmonic is one octave up).

Front: What does phase offset control, and does it change how a signal sounds?
Back: Phase offset sets where in the cycle the wave starts (shift a sine by pi/2 to get a cosine). Changing only the phase does NOT audibly change the sound - the ear is largely phase-insensitive; the magnitude spectrum is unchanged.

Front: Think DSP: signal vs wave vs frame vs sample?
Back: Signal = the mathematical/continuous representation (can be infinite). Wave = the signal evaluated at a discrete sequence of points (finite). Frame = one point in time. Sample = the measured value at that frame (frame/sample used interchangeably).

Front: What is aliasing and what causes it?
Back: Sampling a signal too slowly. A high-frequency component then masquerades as a LOWER frequency - it folds down and appears in the spectrum as a false lower tone at |fs - f|.

Half the sampling RATE: fs/2 (NOT the interval between samples). It is the highest frequency you can faithfully represent. To avoid aliasing, sample at more than twice the highest frequency (fs > 2*f_max).

Front: fs = 44,100 Hz: highest faithful frequency, and what happens to a 30,000 Hz tone?
Back: Nyquist = 22,050 Hz is the highest faithful frequency. 30,000 Hz is above Nyquist, so it aliases: it folds to |44,100 - 30,000| = 14,100 Hz and appears as a false 14.1 kHz tone. (ADCs low-pass filter before sampling to prevent this.)
